result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a wide, multi-lane arterial road with high-speed traffic and minimal separation for walkers. While sidewalks exist, they are narrow and lack safety buffers, and there are no visible marked crossings in the immediate area.

hazards.name: High-speed traffic exposure
hazards.description: Pedestrians on the narrow sidewalk are directly adjacent to multiple lanes of high-speed traffic without any physical buffer or barrier.

hazards.name: Multiple conflict points
hazards.description: Frequent driveway curb cuts for commercial properties create numerous points where turning vehicles cross the pedestrian path.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the roadway near the diner

hazards.name: Long unprotected crossing distance
hazards.description: The wide roadway lacks mid-block crossings or a median refuge, requiring pedestrians to cross five or more lanes of traffic at once.

interventions.title: Road Diet
interventions.description: Reduce the number of travel lanes or narrow existing lanes to slow traffic and provide space for a wider sidewalk buffer or protected bike lanes.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Buffer
interventions.description: Install a planting strip, street trees, or physical barrier between the sidewalk and the roadway to increase pedestrian comfort and safety.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks with pedestrian-activated signals and curb extensions at the nearest intersection to provide safe crossing opportunities.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a continuous sidewalk but lacks a physical buffer from the adjacent roadway. A very wide, undefined parking lot entrance creates a significant conflict zone for pedestrians, while the blank building frontage and lack of street trees contribute to a sterile, auto-oriented atmosphere.

hazards.name: Wide Uncontrolled Driveway
hazards.description: A very wide entrance to a parking lot crosses the sidewalk without clear markings or physical narrowing, creating a large conflict zone between pedestrians and turning vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Center-right, where the sidewalk meets the parking lot entrance.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is directly adjacent to the roadway with no planting strip, parked cars, or physical barrier to protect pedestrians from traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the entire visible length of the sidewalk.

interventions.title: Driveway Consolidation and Narrowing
interventions.description: Reduce the width of the parking lot entrance using curb extensions or tighter corner radii to slow turning vehicles and minimize the distance pedestrians are exposed to traffic.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planting Strip
interventions.description: Install a landscaped buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway to provide physical separation, shade, and a more comfortable walking environment.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Install a marked crosswalk at the location indicated by the existing pedestrian crossing sign to clearly define the pedestrian right-of-way.

result.summary: The environment is dominated by a wide, multi-lane arterial road with no visible pedestrian crossing infrastructure or traffic calming measures. While sidewalks are present on both sides, they are narrow, lack a buffer from high-speed traffic, and are obstructed by utility poles.

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross at least four lanes of traffic without a median or refuge island.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: The narrow sidewalk is directly adjacent to the travel lanes with no physical or horizontal separation.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles are placed within the narrow walking path, reducing effective width.

interventions.title: Road Diet
interventions.description: Reduce the number of travel lanes to include a center turn lane or median, shortening crossing distances and slowing traffic.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median at potential crossing points to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Buffer and Widening
interventions.description: Widen the sidewalk and add a planting strip or furniture zone to separate pedestrians from moving vehicles.

result.summary: The environment is highly car-oriented, featuring a wide multi-lane roadway with no visible pedestrian crossing infrastructure. While a sidewalk exists on the far side, the near side lacks a dedicated walkway, and there is no physical buffer between pedestrians and traffic.

hazards.name: Missing sidewalk
hazards.description: The near side of the street lacks any paved walkway, forcing pedestrians into the roadway or onto unpaved surfaces.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground, near side of the road

hazards.name: Unprotected crossing
hazards.description: Pedestrians wishing to cross the four-lane road have no marked crosswalks or refuge islands, exposing them to traffic over a long distance.

interventions.title: New Sidewalk Construction
interventions.description: Construct a paved sidewalk on the near side of the street to provide a continuous and safe path for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Midblock Pedestrian Crossing
interventions.description: Install a high-visibility marked crosswalk with a pedestrian refuge island to reduce crossing distance and improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Install street lighting to ensure pedestrians are visible to motorists during dawn, dusk, and nighttime.

result.summary: The environment is a wide, multi-lane commercial corridor with basic pedestrian infrastructure including marked zebra crosswalks and signals. However, the lack of physical medians and the significant crossing distance create a high-exposure environment for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic without a refuge island, increasing exposure to vehicle conflicts.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main roadway at the signalized intersection.

hazards.name: Driveway Conflict Points
hazards.description: Wide curb cuts for commercial access create multiple points where turning vehicles cross the pedestrian walkway.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image at the entrance to the auto repair facility.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross the wide roadway in two stages.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at the intersection to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Adjust signal timing to give pedestrians a head start before vehicles receive a green light.

result.summary: The environment features a wide, multi-lane roadway with a continuous sidewalk on the far side, separated from a commercial parking lot by a fence and vegetation.
